# CodexMeter 2.0.3
Every notch provider is now a Settings entry, with its usage in view.
## What changed
- **All notch providers in Settings.** The **Settings ▸ Providers** list used to stop at Codex and Claude Code. It now includes GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Command Code, GLM, Ollama Cloud, and Antigravity — each with a green dot when connected and an "N on" count on the header. - **Usage without opening the notch.** Each borrowed-credential provider's pane, modelled on Codenotch's account row, shows its live limit windows as labelled bars (% used / left, reset time), today's local token total where CodexMeter meters it, any active block, the account the reading is borrowed from, and a per-provider 80% / 100% alert mute. "Allow access…" appears only when macOS actually refused the credential. - Codex and Claude Code keep their fuller panes — they are metered locally.
## Verification
- 592 automated tests, 0 failures (9 environment-integration tests skipped). - `swift build` with zero warnings and zero errors. - Universal 2 build for Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later. - Ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. SHA-256 protects the first download; Sparkle authenticates later updates with Ed25519 signatures.
## Install or update with Homebrew
```bash brew update brew upgrade --cask --greedy dlfkdLR/tap/codexmeter ```
```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CodexMeter.app open /Applications/CodexMeter.app ```
## First direct-download launch
Download `CodexMeter-2.0.3.dmg` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` into the same folder and verify the checksum before opening:
```bash cd ~/Downloads grep ' CodexMeter-2.0.3.dmg$' SHA256SUMS.txt | shasum -a 256 -c - open CodexMeter-2.0.3.dmg ```
## Recovery
This release does not migrate any database. Published version tags are immutable; corrections ship as a new patch release.
